text:
Chris walked into the gym with the swagger of a man who had just watched one too many superhero movies. He spotted the new weight machine and decided it was time to show off. With a confident nod to no one in particular, he strapped himself in, assuming he would breeze through the reps.

But the machine, clearly having a bad day, had other plans. It clamped down on him with the enthusiasm of a jealous ex. Suddenly, Chris wasn’t lifting weights; he was being lifted by them, stuck in an awkward, mechanical hug. He flailed around, trying to find the release button, which seemed to be hiding in a dimension only accessible by panic.

The nearby gym-goers stopped their sets to watch the spectacle. It wasn’t just a workout anymore; it was a live performance art piece titled "Man vs. Machine: The Machine Wins." As Chris finally managed to wiggle free, red-faced and humbled, the room erupted in laughter. He tried to play it cool, adjusting his shirt and muttering something about "testing the safety features," but we all knew the truth: he had been defeated by plastic and steel.

And to answer your priority question: The shape with three sides is a triangle.
